utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Mr. Morrissey, are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Jasarevic, I'm going to move now to another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown the document which is -- it's Defence 65 ter D29. The ERN number is DD00.0084, and it's to be MFI235.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Whilst that's being brought up, Mr. Jasarevic, could I indicate that this document I'm going to show you appears to be a report of sorts from Namik Dzankovic to you, and you mentioned the document yesterday that came to you at some stage in October. And I'll get you to look at this document and then you can tell us about what you see.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And in its Bosnian original, which you have, that's on a single page; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I only see the first half of -- of a half of that page. Actually, I'm seeing the other half of it. But probably if -- I need to see the whole thing to see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Well, your -- feel free to be proactive and explain when you need to see another part of the document. Is that a -- a report by Namik Dzankovic to you, a report compiled by him or dated by him on the 29th of September but received by you at a later time?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And in the lower left corner it says that I received it on the 10th of October, 1993. At the top of the document, you can see the text, my suggestions, tasks. This is written by hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Well, what I have in mind is just to ask you to explain something about the text from -- from Dzankovic and then I want to move forward to -- to ask you some questions about the -- about what you wrote on the document. Just excuse me, please, one moment while I organise myself. Thank you. My apologies. Now, first of all, I'm going to ask you about the text itself from Dzankovic. It appears that at the time he was still on the terrain in Jablanica. Is that in accordance with your recollection of the matter?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't conclude whether he was in Jablanica in that period or not. He probably had to send the document from somewhere, so he probably sent it to them. And you can see at the top which institution he cites where he's sending it from, and it says "IKM of the Supreme Command Staff." That is the place where he sent it from. He had to send it from somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. And it's -- in the text, there are a couple of matters which are referred to which I'd like your comment on, bearing in mind what you said yesterday about the realism or otherwise of his suggestions. Would you look, please, at a paragraph which begins with the words "As concerns eyewitness statements, there are no eyewitnesses here in Jablanica ..." Do you have that part of the text?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it. But allow me before that to say that I would actually just like to give a little contribution. Note the reality. From this document, you can see that Dzankovic does not have certain information at his disposal. For example, he says at the beginning of the text -- could you please scroll the first part of the text down. He begins the sentence: "In the territory of Grabovica," and so on, "a massacre took place," and it says that 30 people lived there. And we know that actually that's the number of people who were killed. And we know that almost 20 people were saved. So this is just one detail indicating that Dzankovic in this respect did not have the proper information. Could we scroll the text up, please, now that -- so that we can see the part of the text that you were referring to. I see that other passage now, which starts: "As far as eyewitness statements are concerned, there are none here in Jablanica." In my opinion, this is a very important moment here. Namely, if 14 adults, two girls, and then those two friends, cousins, son-in-law who was brought there by Mr. Zuka and then they left early -- so we had there a competent 20 person who could be included in the category of eyewitnesses, and of course they're not there on the 29th. It's a pity that this hadn't been done before. This would be a very important and strong detail for the further conduct of the investigation, especially in the pre-criminal part of it. I would just like to point that this is an important moment here, this second part of the passage. Two details are mentioned which are important, in my opinion. Here it is mentioned a name -- actually, the text was underlined by me, this "Samir Pezo" here and the unit which is being accentuated here. Samir Pezo is a person who did certain actions, who prevented the sending and the movement and the participation in combat activities by members of the Croat and Serb nationalities so that they would not be liquidated by members of Celo's assault detachment. This is important. I am saying this here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I certainly want you to go on with your explanation, but I just want to interpose a question here. In your handwritten notes at the top of the page, in English -- you see, we have them all typed out, but on the copy in B/C/S that you have, it's quite clear that you were the person who wrote certain handwritten notes. And I just want to read those out -- because the Tribunal is looking in English, I'll read out those notes and you tell me if this reflects your handwritten notes in the Bosnian language. Your Honours, this is at the top part of the document. "Vahid, give a task to the SVB military service of the 1st Corps to conduct an interview with Samir Pezo and take his statements, send a telegram to Namik" - there's an unclear word there from our point of view - "send a telegram to Namik to return it to the UB," and then some initials follow Now, because we're looking at the English, could I just ask you to confirm that what I've just read out to you constitutes a notation placed on the document later on by you.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, basically it's just as we heard. But I would like to adjust a little bit. But this is the gist of it. I am addressing Vahid - that is the person Vahid Bogunic, who we mentioned before; he is my deputy at my post - where I literally tell him the following: "Task the military service of the 1st Corps to carry out an interview with Semir Pezo and take statement." The second task, since this is already the 10th of October of 1993, is to send a dispatch to him for him to return to the administration because obviously from this function that he was in, as a member of the investigation team or the scout team, and in view of the time that had passed, I felt that there was no longer any need for him to do anything down there. I think that this task, to send a dispatch to Namik to return, probably as far as I remember ensued based on some other documents also, in the sense of ceasing and desisting those activities down there. Otherwise, I wouldn't issue Namik such a task, since he was under the jurisdiction of Mr. Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And although I'm -- I want you to continue with -- with your previous explanation, but just to clarify those two matters. With respect to Dzankovic and his return, the normal course of events is that it would be up to Halilovic to tell him to come back to Sarajevo so long as the inspection team was still in existence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree. I just clarified that. From this distance, I cannot explain that detail, but I feel that by that time the unit had -- units had already returned. So it was probably based on some documents. It was written on the basis of some document, because I didn't have any right to take a person from the inspection team unless there was some grounds for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I'm -- I understand what you say about that, Mr. Jasarevic. And I think there's a document that the Prosecutor either has or -- or I think is intending to tender, a report of the inspection team dated the 20th of September. I'm not -- I don't have it to hand now. Do you recall ever seeing a report from the inspection team dated the 20th of September?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't have that document in my hand, but it's possible that this could also be included in the comment that I provided a little bit earlier on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. Very well. Returning to the first point, then. I notice that you've tasked Vahid with getting the security service of the 1st Corps to interview Pezo. Now, there's two matters I want to ask you about from that. First of all, it wasn't the function of you or your staff at the higher level that you operated to be going and taking statements from individual people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And so what -- what we see here is an appropriate delegation of authority -- sorry, I withdraw that. An appropriate delegation of a function that should really be performed at the corps level, bearing in mind that the 2nd Independent Battalion from which Samir Pezo or to which Samir Pezo belonged -- I'm sorry to say that question got so long I've just completely lost control of it. So let me put it again. What you were doing there was getting the 1st Corps to look after the statement-taking in relation to Pezo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this aim of mine, you can conclude without doubt that we, the administration, were giving this task to the 1st Corps, but we did not insist on the security service of the 1st Corps to take this statement personally. This is a battalion that was directly linked to the 1st Corps. So in that sense, it had the status of a brigade at that level. But the security service of the 1st Corps could regulate that through the security officers of that battalion, because that battalion had its own security officer. So it was up to them to make sure that this statement was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was the SVB representative from the 2nd Independent Battalion in fact Samir Pezo himself?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did I understand you properly? Are you asking me whether Pezo was from the 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking a bit more than that. I'm asking whether it's within your knowledge whether Samir Pezo was from the 2nd Independent Battalion and whether also Samir Pezo was the SVB chief within that independent battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Samir Pezo was from the 2nd Battalion, definitely, and he was an officer with Mr. Adnan Solakovic. I knew their security officer. His nickname was Pike. But I cannot remember the first and last name of that person at the moment. He was lower-ranking, and I didn't meet those people very often. I know that he was an experienced lawyer, and I think that his specialty actually was that he was an attorney --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: If I mention the name to you of Jasmin Panjeta, does that assist?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I'm sorry, because previous to you answering those questions, I -- I interrupted you and you were explaining something about some of the difficulties that you can detect that Namik Dzankovic was -- was encountering in -- in his investigation, which are revealed in that statement. Could I just ask: Did you have something you wanted to add to that, or had you completed that part of the answer?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I look at that second passage of the text again? Yes, that's the one. I was just talking about what we were dealing with right now, about Samir Pezo. There's another detail here which is important and which appears in practically all of the reports from down there, including the one from Dzankovic, and that is to locate the unit that carried out the crime. This is one of the valuable details that can be seen in these -- in this document. It's been underlined. I've said already several times that this was Celo's assault detachment, so this is this other part that I wanted to emphasise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Thank you for that. Would you also look at the final paragraph, please, of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the inquest and all of the work that relates to the exhumation, or before that? I mean before -- I apologise. I mean before that. I mean the sentence before that, the one which says: "It is impossible to get statements from perpetrators or identify them because they returned to Sarajevo immediately after the operation at Vrdi."

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand. Your Honours, I would like to point to something here, which I am actually thinking of constantly and I think that in my testimony I emphasised that before. In my assessment, the crucial factor here is time, time as space, because this remark is such as it is and it is obviously clear. We're talking about the 29th of September, meaning at least 20 days after the crime was committed. And unfortunately that's exactly as it is stated here, that identification of the perpetrators of this act is impossible. And you could see that before that there was a combat operation that was carried out in the hills and so on, which again coincides with this wish to -- not to stop the combat activities, implying -- and where it was implied that the conduct of an inquiry would stop the combat activities, this is the other detail that probably made Mr. Delalic condition the whole thing, and this is one detail. I am noting it and I am emphasising it and I believe that it is important.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Are you aware of any occasion when the pre-criminal phase of a murder investigation has been carried out in the middle of a combat operation? Has that ever occurred, in your experience?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Luckily we've never encountered such a situation, such an obvious situation as that. But a little earlier I wanted to emphasise that I am sure we are all aware what an on-site investigation means, or a crime scene examination, and that is when we all have the elements that are necessary to conduct a proper investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, my final question about this document relates to the very final sentence in it, and that's the sentence concerning exhumation and on-site investigation. You see there -- Mr. Dzankovic appears to say: "It has been agreed that the on-site investigation will be carried out by the crime service of the MUP and the Jablanica military police in cooperation with other professionals." Now, he refers to an agreement which has obviously already been made, and what I want to ask you is: Do you know about that? And if you do know about it, what are the details of that agreement to which he refers?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, you can see from this that Mr. Dzankovic writing such reports uses terms and notes things which actually deviate from the proper terms and are not quite clear. In this passage, he knows that -- he notes good things. It's good that this action will be carried out, the exhumation, and that this will be carried out by the expert services. However, I -- or to me, as a soldier, the term "agreed" is not adequate. Probably it reflected the true situation. But I would prefer for him to have used a term such as "it has been ordered," "regulated," so that then we could see who this was done, who was the one who reached this agreement. It's okay, what it says "the crimes department and military police units in cooperation with other experts," meaning maybe the medical staff or something. So I -- it seems to me as if something is being assumed or concluded here that is not actually contained here. In any case, this action, such as -- as an action is okay here, and as far as -- and it's good he reported on it -- and as far as I know, I think this exhumation was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That was going to be my next question. Do you know who by and when?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was too long ago for me to remember when and by whom, but done professionally and within a reasonable amount of time. This is something that I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And bearing in mind the -- the issues of memory there, can you recall whether any such information was available once -- to investigators once the operation of Trebevic commenced on the 26th of October, or can you not recall that at this length of time?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I request not remember that, especially because Trebevic was carried out in a methodology involving teams which each had their own tasks and then several institutions were used there. At least four or five institutions took part in the implementation of that operation, so that -- albeit that this could be an important fact, I really couldn't remember any -- any particulars well enough to be able to comment on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And just in conclusion about that. The -- the phrase used by Dzankovic there is "it has been agreed that the on-site investigation and exhumation work will be carried out by the crime service of the MUP." And I just want to ask you about the on-site investigation part of that component. I should ask you, first of all: Was it necessary that you be briefed about that on-site investigation that's referred to there? And secondly, if -- if you were briefed about it, what can you tell us about it, if anything?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't important or necessary to brief me on this question for several reasons, because I was physically absent and I was at such a level that objectively in practice I would not give such briefings. Other than the things that preceded this document, the directive that was sent on the 21st where de facto this document ensued as a reaction, as a response to that security service administration document which was sent to Dzankovic on the 21st.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And bearing in mind what you said about the -- that it would be desirable that Dzankovic record some sort of order being issued, in terms of the agreement mentioned there, is it possible to say by looking at that last sentence there whether the MUP was -- well, perhaps I withdraw that. Who was coordinating the work between the MUP and the SVB? Is it possible to determine, in other words, who was controlling that aspect of the investigation?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot really locate that now. At that level, somebody should have coordinated it, but it would have been the most usual thing for the command of the operation to coordinate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. In short, is it fair to summarise Dzankovic's efforts in this way: He appears to have acted with goodwill but lacking certain expertise? Is that a fair comment from a professional assessment level?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think absolutely that Dzankovic wanted to do whatever he could do at the time, without even thinking whether he was competent formally with regard to his position on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I offer that document for tender.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I now have to move to some other documents that are a little more remote but are still documents that perhaps may say something about how the investigation unfolded. And this is all in the time before Trebevic began on the 26th of October. As I've indicated, I'm into the last part of the cross-examination now, so I just have to ask you about those, a couple of very old documents from a time before that, and then I've finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please now be shown a document -- this is 65 ter number D488. Sorry. Just excuse me one moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: This is another document which will have to be dealt with in paper form. Your Honours, we have copies for everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, this, like many other documents, is one you may or may not have seen in recent times. Would you mind just having a look at that document and note the dates of it and note who it's from and then indicate whether you understand that you received that document. Whilst looking at it, could I indicate that although I made my qualification about documents being a little more remote, I -- I jumped the gun there really by one document. This one seems to be directly in the line of -- of documents that we have been looking at. But you look through it and then tell us what you recall about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours. I neglected to indicate this would be MFI236.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have never seen this document before. I cannot claim that it was never seen before one of my colleagues in the administration, because I can see here that it was addressed to the security sector. This was not its name. It was the Department of the Military Security Services of the 6th Corps. This is crossed by hand and then replaced by "the 6th Corps for the attention of Jusuf Jasarevic" - that was me - "And then chief Nermin Eminovic." I don't remember ever having seen this document before, and I have to remind you that every time I received a document I would put in my own handwriting instructions to my subordinates as to what they were supposed to do with regard to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that. And it may be -- well, it certainly will be the case that we shall ask questions to Chief Nermin Eminovic about this document. But just -- could you indicate using your professional experience and knowledge whether or not this document arrived at your Sarajevo headquarters, and if so, at what time did it arrive -- well, sorry, on what date did it arrive there.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is another indicator showing that if it had arrived at the staff, it would have borne the stamp indicating the date of receipt. Somebody would have received it. It was a common practice. As things stand now, I can't tell you any more specific and claim with any more certainty that it did arrive or that it didn't arrive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. I just want to ask you a couple of questions about information known to you. Can you confirm whether or not from your own knowledge that information concerning a Croatian soldier, Slavko Mendes, was communicated through organs of the 6th Corps to -- to your office and, in particular, that information concerning how Slavko Mendes actually came to be killed was communicated to your office? And I understand that you say that -- you -- you've indicated that you didn't receive this particular document or you can't recall doing so. But leave that aside. Do you recall that actual information about Slavko Mendes reaching your level or reaching you, in fact?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall whether or not it was indicated to you that by way of explanation for what happened in Uzdol, that there had been fierce fighting in the village and that civilians had actually participated in that fighting?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had this information from -- special information that I signed, and that was drafted by our Department for Analysis based on documents that they had received. I'm familiar with that. I signed the document, and before that I had familiarised myself with the contents of that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And just following from that, is that one of the documents that you looked at yesterday or is it another document that we haven't produced in this court that you're now referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document we saw yesterday, and we looked at it last -- its last paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and commented upon it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. I understand that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I offer this document for tender. I offer that document for tender, noting, however, that the witness has not identified it himself, so if a different argument needs to be advanced about why it's appropriate we'll do that at a later stage. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, another short document which is somewhat remote from these matters but has a potential relevance anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown now -- this is ERN number D480, and it's -- sorry, pardon me. That's -- its 65 ter number was D480(a), and its ERN number is DD00.2203, and it will be MFI237.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Whilst this is just being brought up, I'll indicate to you what's coming. It's a document that appears to be an instruction or order by you concerning the Pazaric incident which you gave evidence about some time ago now. Do you have that document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, is that document what it appears to be; namely, a task assigned by you to the chief of the 1st Corps military security service to collect evidentiary material and initiate criminal proceedings against the perpetrators of that particular offence?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, this is my document. I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And yes, this is okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And the chief of the military security service, is that a man called Sacir Arnautovic?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I looked at the date. That's why I halted for a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I offer that for tender as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What's the MFI number?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's MFI237.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, the next document to which I'd like to direct your attention is now a late -- no, sorry, this is a document -- it's an SDT -- it's an SDB document from the MUP, but I just want you to comment, if you can comment, on a couple of aspects of it. Could the witness please be shown ERN number D170 -- sorry, 65 ter number D170. The ERN number is DD00.0782, and it's to be MFI238.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, this document is not being put to you as being your document. It's signed by a different person altogether. But I wanted to ask you first of all: Did that document come -- come into the possession of your organisation as part of the operative information -- the flow of operative information which you discussed earlier on?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I please look at the beginning of this document? This is my handwriting. I am issuing a task to Goran. This is Goran Radovic, a lawyer at the administration. And another task to the service for analysis. Again, this is my handwriting but there are no -- my initials. My initials are missing after these remarks. Looking at the date, it is obvious that I had this document in my hands, especially in view of the handwritten part of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And does it appear -- now, could you just explain to the Court who Jozo Jozic was or is -- sorry, what his role was at that time, and which it was he came from, whether he's from the civilian side or from the military side.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jozo Jozic was the chief of the State Security of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the Ministry of the Interior. The MUP was divided into public and state security, and the MUP police was under the public security; whereas, the SDB was the more specific or special part that dealt with intelligence and counter-intelligence. And the head of that part, of that institution, was Mr. Jozo Jozic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And at that time, was his supervising minister, the Minister of the Interior, Bakir Alispahic?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the questions here really concern -- are really about the concerns expressed in this document as relevant to you. Does it -- is -- perhaps I'll put the question another way. Is the information contained in that document consistent with the information you had received from Dzankovic and Eminovic and consistent with the impression you had formed generally speaking about the difficulties of investigating this matter at Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It reflects only one part of the problems that we had received information about from Dzankovic and Salihamidzic and partly from Eminovic. It gives two or three more important things that in principle coincide.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Could I ask you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I offer that document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could I just ask you: In that seven weeks between the committing of the killings at Grabovica and the commencement of Trebevic -- Operation Trebevic on the 26th of October, did you ever hear that members of the 2nd Independent Battalion were prepared to talk or were prepared to make statements or assist the investigation in any way?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I don't understand. You're referring to the 6th Battalion, but I believe that you mean the 6th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I think we got -- all of us got confused at that point. I was referring to the 2nd Independent Battalion, a unit contained within the 1st Corps but a unit which had been on the battlefield in Herzegovina and elements of which had been present in Grabovica when the killings took place. And my question really is this: Bearing in mind what your role was and the fact that you were somewhat removed from the immediate investigation, nevertheless do you recall hearing whether or not the 2nd Independent Battalion or any members of it were prepared to talk, were prepared to help, were prepared to make statements?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can't remember this. However, in my answer, I rely on the suggestion that I regularly received to get -- to inform the chief of security of the 1st Corps, who was superior to the security service of this battalion. And in practical matters, this should have been their task. The second thing on which I base my answer is the instruction that we have just seen in which Pezo Samir is highlighted as having been given a very concrete task or instruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: This may not be in your knowledge, but if it is, I'll ask you to tell us: Did the investigators get a statement from Samir Pezo before Trebevic commenced on the 26th of October? In other words, did they succeed in getting a statement from him?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jasarevic. Now I move to three documents that may or may not have come to your attention in their entirety. And I just want to show them to you one after another here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: First of all, a document with ERN number DD00.0425, and that will become MFI239. I think, Your Honours, can I indicate by my count now there are six documents to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Does that document appear? Now, would you just have a look at that document. It may be the case that this document was seen by you and it may be the case that it wasn't, but I'd just like you to inspect it and to see -- and comment. And just so that you understand what the questions are about, I'm going to show you this document, which is a document said to be signed by Alija Izetbegovic, and then there are two following documents that appear to be under the signature - if you agree they are, of course - of Rasim Delic, and they are effectively correspondence about the matters arising from inquiries by Mr. Tadeus Mazovjecki at that time. Now, my first question about this D106 document is: Have you ever seen this document yourself?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: My second question is: Did you become aware at any time whether or not -- at around this date, at around the 17th of October, did you become aware as to whether or not the president himself was seeking clarification of certain matters at the behest of Mr. Tadeus Mazovjecki, who was the UN special reporter for human rights in the territory of former Yugoslavia. In other words, did you become aware, whether you saw the letter or not, that the president was making these inquiries in order to be able to speak to Mr. Mazovjecki about these matters??

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. In general terms, do you recall whether or not there was an issue of an inquiry being made by the UN special rapporteur at that time? Do you recall that as an issue arising at some stage in late October of 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I offer that document. And I note also that there will be an argument focussed on a basis that's not the usual one in relation to this, because he's quite clearly given a -- he's given -- the witness has given a clear answer about it. But the matters may arise in another way, and so I'm going to persist with offering them and I'll put an argument in support of it later. Very well. Now, the next document is a related document which may meet the same fate, but we'll see. It's 65 ter number D107, ERN number DD00. -- Sorry, I take away that dot, DD000431, and it will be MFI240.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The document that's about to be shown to you appears to be signed -- or has a signature on it saying "Rasim Delic." It's dated the 17th of October, and it's directed to the -- to the 6th Corps command. It doesn't have a name, but it's directed to the 6th Corps command. And although it doesn't contain any explicit reference or any reference that I can see to your organisation, I just want to ask you whether or not this document did pass -- did go through your hands at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, again, judging by the customary markings on the document, I don't remember ever having held this document in my hands. However, looking at the contents of the document, the title, and the addressee, in a certain way I can establish a link. I don't claim that. However, I can establish a link the way we insisted on certain documents yesterday which from the military security administration were sent to the military security of the 6th Corps asking them to send this information that they had about the incident in the Prozor sector. It is possible that there is a link between that problem and those requests. However, I am absolutely certain that I did not have this document in my hands, because I know exactly how I would have reacted had it been in my hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I offer that document on the same unusual basis, and I make it clear that that document, and the one to follow, are all in exactly the same boat, assuming that the witness gives the same answer with this one. Finally could the witness please be shown 65 ter number D108. This is DD000433, and it will be MFI241.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, with respect to this document, the subject matter again is, quite frankly, remote, but it may be related to the other documents and that's why I ask you the question: Have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the first part of the page, I believe that I didn't, but I'd like to see the complete document, please. This document as such was never in my hands. Under, too, you can see -- firstly at the bottom, it was customary to put who the document is referred to or who it is sent to. Since there is no such indicator, there is no written reaction to the document on my behalf, so I can conclude that this document was never in my hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I offer that for tender in the same way and on the same basis as the other two to which the same arguments would apply.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. I'm sorry. Now, I just have, I think, three or four more to go, just depending on your answer to the next one, really. I would like now, please, to show you one -- two documents from older history, back earlier in 1993. These relate to -- one relates to the individual known as Celo, Ramiz Delalic; the other two are Caco, Musan Topalovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown -- it's Defence ERN -- sorry, Defence 65 ter number D509. It is DD002386, and it will be ERN number 242 -- MFI number 242, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'll explain while that's being brought up what you're about to be shown. This is a transcript -- it's said to be a transcript of a telephone conversation. The Defence is not warranting that it's genuine, bona fide, or legally obtained, but the document may have passed across your desk, and so I'd ask you to look firstly to see whether you ever received any such thing, and it passed across your desk. And then if -- depending on your answer to that, we'll ask some further questions about it. As you read it, could I just explain something about it and what I particularly want you to look at -- or well, first of all, could I ask you the formal question and we'll get into the contents of it in a minute. This seems to be addressed to personally, Mr. Jusuf Jasarevic, and it's dated the 12th of February, 1993. So it's quite early in 1993. And it's a -- it purports to be, anyway, a transcript of a telephone conversation which contains operative information which may or may not have a word of truth in it but nevertheless is operative information. Can I ask you whether you did in fact receive that document and whether it passed over your desk or through your department.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that. I'm speaking about that suggestion of mine again which I gave. This is the 12th of February, 1993. I was not the number-one man at that time. And you can absolutely see that this was addressed to me, but I don't recall having this document in my hands. I cannot see who it's from. I don't know at the end -- it has some sort of code, "0028." I cannot really identify by that who it was who sent the document. I can't really give you any further information about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'll see if you can -- I'm just going to read a passage to you, and you tell me if this assists your memory or not as to whether this passed across your desk. It seems to be a discussion between an individual -- or one individual and another person called Juka. And in that discussion --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the English translation, it's on page 2, about 12 or 13 lines from the -- from the bottom of the page. One second, sorry. We're just going to locate it in the Bosnian version, Mr. Jasarevic, if you'd just bear with me for one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. It's about seven lines from the bottom, maybe eight lines or so from the bottom, is the passage that I'm going to take you to -- 11 lines from the bottom, I'm told. Okay. There's a passage that says: "Bozo tells Juka about some apparatuses in the cellar and Sefica [phoen] listens to it and says that six new cafes are going to be opened, to which Juka replies, "And so they should be." I'm sorry, I'm reading from an earlier passage there. I'll move on from that. Juka asks, "Did you take that thing from Nago," that's interposed Dr. Nago, the logistics person. The answer is, "Yes, he is doing something for you and he is God," says Sefica. Celo said, "I swear upon my child I will kill him." Sefer: "Even if the whole town police is guarding him, Juka said he should do it before it's too late and I will get him sooner or later." And then it goes on to talk about Coca-Cola. Was it within your knowledge at that time in February of 1993 that there was a tape-recording or at least a transcript of a telephone conversation where the possibility of Celo killing Sefer was mentioned?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a very serious thing, and this is something that definitely would warrant a response. This name "Juka," this document actually refers to Jusuf Prazina, called Juka. This document, I've seen this now, this text, indicating this about Mr. Sefer, probably meaning Mr. Sefer Halilovic, who at the time was the number-one man in the army. Of course, this would warrant a response. I doubt that I ever had such a document in my hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. Excuse me. And also, you can see at the beginning of the document that the receiving stamp is not from the administration. This is not an administration stamp. It's very characteristic and it appeared on several documents of ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What -- what does the stamp at the top indicate as to where this document was received? In other words, who got it?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "Supreme Command Staff." I don't know whether that's the cabinet of the commander or the Chief of the Main Staff at the time. I don't know if that's their stamp or the stamp of some other organ in the general affairs office and so on. I really cannot specify or say anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, bearing that in mind, I'll limit my questions to one final question. Does this appear to be, without saying whether it's true, false, or -- or any other status, does this just appear to be operative information that's flowed through the system or a system of intelligence-gathering at some point?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, from my first or earlier response, you can understand this response also: Operative information probably came to where it was supposed to come, and this information was so serious that it warranted a serious response.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness now be shown -- sorry, I offer that document for tender.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object to this particular document at this stage because the Prosecution hasn't had an opportunity to give detailed consideration and neither have we been told where is it from. Just looking at it now, Your Honour, there seems to be a lot more in this document, and we would like an opportunity to give a detailed consideration, as I said earlier. And then in the event -- perhaps in my re-examination bring it up and see whether we actually object to it or not. But at this stage I certainly will be objecting to it. And, Your Honour, this is indicative of the -- the problem that we do not have these documents in advance. Your Honour, I've invited Your Honours to revisit this particular issue, and this is exactly the kind of thing we are trying to forestall. But these things are bounced upon us. It is a telephone transcript. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You don't -- you don't have all the documents with the witness's name at your hands, I suppose?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I need to respond to that. This document has an ERN number on it of 01861864. My learned friend I'd have no objection to her seeking whatever time she needs to respond, as she always has. Your Honours, I'm cross-examining now, and I don't want to interrupt that by responding, but you're seeing a tactic here which is quite clear, and in my submission there's a clear ruling in place. There's a proper way for my learned friend to deal with the ruling that Your Honours have made. My friend is now -- has now on repeated occasions sought to disturb that ruling every time she makes an objection. And frankly, there will be a proper time to do that. I don't seek to say that she's got a good argument, a bad argument, or no argument. It's not the appropriate time to do this. Could we deal with it at another time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Let's finish your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: First.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Okay. Well, I simply offer that document for tender. And in the future it's -- that question will be determined. Thank you. Now, could the witness please be shown 65 ter number D521(a). It is DD002425, and it will be MFI243.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The document that you're now to be shown is an order signed by Sefer Halilovic, and it's one which you -- I'll ask you to look at and -- and consider when it comes up.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: There seems to be a problem. I cannot locate the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I -- there's another document I can turn to, but I really have got just two documents to go and then I'm going to finish, Your Honour, so I haven't got anything to pad out the -- the moments with, frankly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just take the opportunity to have a look at that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I indicate the English version is two pages and the -- the final marking of Sefer Halilovic is on the second of the pages. The substance of the order is on the first and the Halilovic name is on the second.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. What does that appear to be, Mr. Jasarevic?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the application of combined methods from the domain of the security service, from item 5 of the security service rules, where the immediate superior in the army -- to him the implementation of that method is suggested or proposed to him, because that are activities which exceed the bounds of certain regulations about the inviolability of privacy and so on. You can also see the explanation for the proposal, then the proposal itself, and the document ends by suggesting who would actually implement these measures. This is sa period when -- this is a period when I was not at the head of the administration, and I'm not sure whether this was implemented or not. I can see in the last part Mr. Sefer Halilovic in his capacity as Chief of the Main Staff or the number-one man in the army approved the application of this method and said that the security service of the 1st Corps should implement it. This is something that I'm not familiar with and this document is not something that I am knowledgeable about. It's my opinion, but I cannot be certain, that these activities in the technical sense are something that the 1st Corps security service could not have carried out by itself without close cooperation with the State Security Service. But since this is not my document, I cannot really be competent to discuss it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, I -- I understand what you say, and I'm going to limit my questions to a couple of matters. Fikret Muslimovic was your predecessor at the -- as head of the SVB; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: This order is regular in form in that although Muslimovic was capable of proposing such measures, they had to be signed off on by a commander, and at that time the commander of the army was Sefer Halilovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was not the name of the post but he was the man, number one. He was the Chief of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And just finally, in terms of that document: What do the stamps tell you about -- what -- are there any markings on that document that indicate whether that document was present in the -- in the SVB offices, or was received there or originated there?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the top left-hand corner, you can see the words "security administration," and then you have the number "03/" and the rest is empty. That is actually the ID number where -- or the number of the record where this document was recorded. I don't see any other markings. I don't see any stamps, only the signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So does it -- does that number there indicate that the document was received and filed but you can't say any more about it than that, or have I got that wrong?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has some omissions. There is no record number, and there are no stamps over any of the signatures; namely, the signature of Mr. Fikret Muslimovic and Mr. Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There is a handwritten number "369" there. Are you able to indicate whether that appears to be a later addition or whether it's a -- an addition made by somebody filing a document? Do you see the document -- the number "369" right in the middle at the top?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And I can indicate to the Court that the words "Dok. Br. 521-A" are Defence -- Halilovic Defence notations made at a much later time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That 369 I just want to ask whether that means anything to you, Mr. Muslimovic -- sorry, Mr. Jasarevic. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't really mean anything to me. It doesn't really ring any bells.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Is it consistent with being a filing number, or are you unable to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I cannot comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I offer that document for tender as well. The final document I wish to show is a -- a transcript which you may or may not have seen but on which you may nevertheless be able to comment. This is 65 ter number D400. It is DD001744, and it will be MFI244.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, what you have in front of you here is a transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, this -- sorry, this is -- sorry, this is a document that was provided to the Defence pursuant to Rule 68 disclosure materials by the Prosecutor, and it bears an ERN number on it, 01322558.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What you have is a transcript. Feel free to -- to look at the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could we have the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You should have, Your Honour. It's ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The second -- the part that I'm most interested in is on the second page of this document, both in English and in B/C/S, Your Honours. And here President Izetbegovic says, "You know we have made one more move." The President Tudjman says, "What kind of move?" Izetbegovic says, "You know, the changes we made." And the President, "I don't know, I came back from a trip today and I don't know while I was away." Alija Izetbegovic says, "So you -- this has to remain between us, of course. It needn't by like that now. We moved Halilovic, you know. There were complaints that he might not want peace with the Croats, that he was not implementing the agreements, that he was maybe even obstructing them." The president asks, "Moved where?" And Alija Izetbegovic observes, "Moved. He's not a commander any more." And the president says, "So what is he?" And Alija Izetbegovic says, "formally he's the Chief of Staff, but I think, it seems to me, you know -- you know, he isn't. He can retain some professional duties, but he will not conduct talks. He will not command units. He will not issue orders. He cannot issue an order to go into action anywhere. He cannot do anything. Perhaps we cannot remove a man who did fight after all. We do not have reliable facts." Now, there's more after that which may be of relevance, and if you feel the need to read it, feel -- please -- please do so. But that's the part I wish to comment on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: This is a document, Your Honours, dated the 11th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, my first question to you is: As a matter of form, have you ever seen this specific document before?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Secondly, again, a question of form: Were you aware that the Presidency -- that tape recordings were kept - I'm not suggesting kept by you - that tape recordings were routinely made of presidential meetings of this nature? Perhaps I should withdraw that question now. Something has just been drawn to my attention there. The question should be rephrased: Were you aware that the -- the meetings of the Croatian Presidency were routinely taped?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Were you broad -- well, were you aware that President Izetbegovic communicated in this way to President Tudjman on the 11th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what date did you come -- was it the 17th of July that you came to occupy the position of leadership of the SVB?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. In the position that you occupied before that time, did you have occasion to learn of the contents of these discussions between the president of Bosnia and the president of Croatia in the term which is have been provided by the Prosecution to the Defence in this case?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you thinking of these talks between the presidents of Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina? I'm sorry, I don't know if I understood the question properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. That is what I was asking you, whether you were aware of the contents of the discussions between those precise individuals.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Nevertheless, Your Honour, I still offer that matter for tender, argument to be put about it in due course. Mr. Jasarevic, thank you for your patience. Those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's high time for a break, and we will have 30 minutes' break. We'll resume at quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm sorry for the delay. Ms. Chana, your redirect examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Jasarevic. I will now ask you a few questions as a matter of clarification from issues which -- which arose as a result of the Defence's cross-examination. I'd appreciate it, Mr. Jasarevic, if you would sort of keep your answers belief because this is basically clarifications, and they're not -- not in any particular order. I've just followed the order that the questions were asked during cross-examination. Now, one of the first questions you were asked was in respect of the Trebevic operation, and you were asked whether Defence counsel could characterise it as a goal. Now, would you clarify that for us, Mr. Jasarevic. Was it an operation, a military operation, or were these just shared goals?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that wasn't the question at all, and it's -- it's putting the matter misleadingly, in my submission, to do it that way. As I recall the situation, what the witness said was that -- there was a meeting of a -- of a Council for the Protection of the Constitutional Order. At that meeting, a number of persons formed an agreement. I termed -- characterised it as goals. Later on the term "Trebevic" came to be used. If there's something arising out of that, I have no objection. But that was the way I put the question, as I recall it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think there's no problem with Ms. Chana's question.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: So would you call that a shared goal or would you call that a military operation?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is not a military operation in terms of it being a combat operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: We appreciate it wasn't a combat operation, but what kind of an operation would this be? First of all, would it be a goal or would it be an operation? And then we can go into the kind of operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: He hasn't answered the question, Your Honour, as to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, I know, Your Honours. But look, this has got to proceed seriously at the start. Now, that's a leading question. If you look at the last part of it -- would it -- first of all, would it be a goal or would it be an operation? And then my friend says, "And then we can go on to see what kind of operation." It's just the leadingest of leading questions, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, let's use the word "operation" first.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Then we'll come to the goal.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: The question -- the initial question was the -- the operation. Was it -- you've just said it was not a military operation but it was nevertheless an operation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I -- but when I said that this was not a military operation, I was thinking in combat terms, that this was not a military operation. The goal of that operation was to deal with the illegal behaviour and action of the units of the 1st Corps that we mentioned. This was the essence. This was the main objective.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And was this operation conceived before the murders in Grabovica and Uzdol or after?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a prior idea to deal with the problem of the lack of discipline. This was all accelerated by the crimes in Grabovica, and this then spread on to the Operation Neretva 93.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: So the -- the indiscipline of the troops was the reason why this operation was launched, which was prior to the Grabovica murders and Uzdol murders? You'd confirm that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, look, the topic is relevant, but there has to be no leading. Can I indicate I'm going to continue to object to leading questions. This topic is relevant. My friend can ask about it. But there just can't be any leading questions. The witness has to be given the chance to answer as he sees fit. It's an important --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: -- Principle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may ask what is the reason for that operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was just summing up what the witness had said basically, so ...

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: In -- when my learned friend questioned you on this aspect, he put it to you that Trebevic was to investigate the crimes in Grabovica. Was that the purpose of Operation Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was one of the tasks. Actually, the main tasks -- the main task, which determined the speed and the form of that operation. If there hadn't been these crimes, maybe it would not have been called what it was called, and it is dubious whether it would have contained all the elements of implementation that it had.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: What if there had been no crimes committed? Would it have still continued?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only assume that it would continue, but I don't know whether the intensity of it would have been the same, whether it would have taken place at that particular moment and whether it would have been implemented in the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes. Now, getting away from this for a moment. You said in line 31:16, and I'm quoting, that "MUP security managed to compile more valuable and greater amounts of such information." Now, this was in relation to -- to information-gathering generally and the operative information that you've been talking about. Do you remember that, Mr. Jasarevic?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, obviously you've been shown a lot of documents and there's been a lot of operational information in these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Did you have any reason to believe that a lot of this information was accurate or inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I object to that question. Not only did it not require clarification, because the witness made his position quite clear about what operative information was, but in cross-examination I didn't seek to disturb that, and I didn't seek to get from him that any of it was true or wasn't true, since it was clear what his answer was. To represent that as a matter of clarification, in my submission, is not correct and it's not a question that arises from cross-examination; therefore, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, my problem is that this question is too general, you know. It's kind of a generalisation, you know, for all the information contained in those documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's just that the witness was asked this very question in -- in these -- in these sort of general terms, and it's the general reply that the witness gave, and I'm quoting - it's at line 31:16, page 31, and 16:14:58. I'm not sure whether we need to go back to the transcript, but I will perhaps ask it in another way, Your Honour, if that's acceptable to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think you just quoted that "The MUP security managed to compile a more valuable and greater amount of such information."

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And I'm just asking about this information, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: When you said that the MUP and state security managed to compile more valuable and greater amounts of such information, can you please tell the Court what you were talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this was indicia, and this information was indicative in terms of what it contained. In the security administration, we found it important who the information came from, and it came from -- from the state security, which was a very competent institution, and there was also similar information that came with less detail from the corps, from the 1st Corps and from the 4th Corps, if I can remember well.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Jasarevic. Now, you were asked whether you could have foreseen the killings at Grabovica by the learned Defence counsel, and you replied, "I was shocked about the crimes committed in Grabovica." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Were you shocked about the crimes and also about the units or one or the other? Committed them. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Primarily the crimes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Were you shocked about the units which committed those crimes?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able -- be able to say that I was shocked, Your Honours. This is a too-strong word for me.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: So what would you use? What word would you use?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that one could expect from these units to behave in a way which goes beyond the terms of military discipline; however, it was hard to assume that it might even commit crimes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Did you have information about these particular units having committed crimes in the past from your operative information work?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'll object to that. This is an attempt to recommence evidence in chief. Of course he had such information. He's given long evidence about it, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. And we also see some documents about --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- you know, those incidents.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: That's right. I was merely confirming that from the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, there's nothing to confirm about if the witness has already answered that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I will move right along then.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, the other question counsel for the Defence asked you was that persuasion was the chief way of dealing with matters. He was talking about how you were persuading certain brigade commanders and -- because you did not have the authority to issue orders. And you said -- you had agreed with the Defence counsel that persuasion was one of the techniques that you yourself used. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that this is absolutely correct; however, I did confirm that did use that technique, and I even gave you some examples. The circumstances called for flexibility in order to achieve the effects and the goals that you wanted to achieve under the circumstances, in the state of war, and all that the war entailed. On the other hand, one had to bear in mind the level of education of some of the officers in order to understand that this was a necessity.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes. But did persuasion replace orders?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I was not authorised to issue orders. I was not an order-issuing person.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: But those who were order-issuing persons, would they use persuasion or would they use orders?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commanders were those who issued orders. They did not use persuasion. I used this word conditionally to explain the kind of practice that was in place as an exception and that explained the way we lived. In those conditions, we did what we could under the circumstances, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you for that. The other issue that learned counsel asked you about was whether all the other units, other than the 9th and 10th, were also in some way involved in criminal actions or lack of discipline. And -- but the question in respect of -- my question in respect of that would be: Did you get as many reports about other units as you did about the 9th and 10th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Did you have to have a similar operation like -- that you did Trebevic in respect of the 9th and the 10th for any other units in the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I -- no. If this had been necessary, I'm sure that it would have been done.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Did you find that to be quite unusual, that you have to have an operation against the BiH, its own troops?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. It was a necessary evil. It was an extremely huge problem for us. Well, this was just like opening of the third front. Actually, it could have been that if it hadn't ended the way it did.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, I want to talk about digging trenches. And you answered to a question put by learned counsel that, "Digging trenches was not a crime." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, would it be a crime to forcibly take civilians to dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the conditions that we had in place -- when you say "crime," I mean murders and forceful taking people away does contain a certain element of illegal action, but not crime per se, if my interpretation is good.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: You said you -- "When you say 'crime', I mean murders." There are other crimes other than murders, to your knowledge, are there?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And what would forcible taking of civilians? What kind of crimes would you envisage those might be?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the current state of affairs is that he didn't concede that it was a crime at all. Again, it's just an example of -- well, sorry, no speeches. I object because it misrepresents what is the witness himself said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. The witness said that taking people away does contain a certain element of illegal action but not a crime per se.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. But if I look at the transcript, he says, "When you say crime, I mean murders."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And I was trying to clarify that there's other -- other criminal activity other than murders that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: There's no problem. There's no problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And I was asking him if he -- what kind of criminality would he envisage when you forcibly take civilians to dig trenches. To his --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And he has answered that question. He said that there's an element of illegal acts, you know, in these kind of actions.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, work platoons were also discussed during your -- during your cross-examination, and you said yes, that work platoons were something that were used to dig trenches as it was very important to dig trenches in Sarajevo, which is understandable because of the siege. Now, is there -- was there a difference between forcibly taking people to dig trenches and these work platoons?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And what is this difference, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When platoons were established, this was done in an organised, legal way, and forcibly taking people to do that contains elements of force and -- and hence the difference, a huge difference.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'll come to another area which you were questioned on, and that is security assessment of an area where an operation is to be conducted, a military operation. What is the role of a commander of an operation in security assessment?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I object to that. The witness wasn't -- wasn't examined in chief about this topic, and he wasn't cross-examined about what the role of the commander was in respect to a military operation, as I recall it. There were certainly questions about -- there were questions of -- about the role of a commander in particular circumstances. I concede that. But this -- what I'm objecting to here is the term of "the military operation," about which the witness himself gave some clear answers as to his knowledge and he was clear about it. So I may not object to a similar type of question, but I'm concerned about the issue of operation, because frankly I'd submit that both the answer is clear and, further, I didn't ask those questions about the -- the commander of a -- of a operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Can you rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This would be at page 68 of the transcript, Your Honour, where the security assessment ...

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Who is primarily responsible for doing a security assessment in an area where a military operation is to be conducted?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The security organ of the command that conducted the combat operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Upon whose orders?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the commander who runs the entire process, and the command is a joint body consisting of several people, several joint organs. The security organ consisted of at least two or three people.
